product.name: Velociti
product.one_liner: The AI operating system for product management. A PM walks in with an idea and walks out with validated strategy and shippable work — in one session.

Velo AI generates the canvas, problem map, story map and initiatives, then turns prioritized initiatives into user stories, Jira-ready backlog tickets, working web-app prototypes and Context PRDs on one click. work_experience.description: Owns the surfaces where Velociti's promise is either kept or broken: the first ninety seconds a trial user judges the product on, the Velo AI drawer where the agent has to visibly earn its keep, and the export path that converts AI output into tickets a team actually ships. Works the full width of the stack — most onboarding, auth and AI-agent UX on the React frontend, and follows a feature straight through the FastAPI/LangGraph agents backend and the Supabase Postgres/Edge Function layer rather than stopping at the API boundary.
work_experience.simple_summary: I work as a Software Engineer at VelocitiPM, on a tool called Velociti that helps product managers focus on what actually matters instead of getting buried in busywork — it turns a product idea into a validated plan and ready-to-ship work automatically. I'm mainly a frontend developer, but I also work on the backend and manage the database. On the frontend, I redesigned the sign-up and login experience, the onboarding flow, and the AI assistant panel so it feels trustworthy and easy to use. On the backend and database side, I connect those same features to the data layer and set up automation so that when one part of the product changes, related parts update on their own. Overall, I take a feature from the screen the user sees all the way down to the database, instead of just working on one piece of it.
simple_highlights: Redesigned the sign-up, login, and onboarding experience so new users understand the product faster.
Improved the AI assistant panel so it feels reliable and clearly shows what it's doing.
Simplified how AI-generated results turn into tickets, so teams can act on them faster.
Connected frontend features to the backend and database so status updates flow through automatically.
Work across the full stack — frontend, backend, and database — rather than staying in just one layer.
highlights: Rebuilt the entire front door. A trial user decides in ninety seconds whether Velociti gets a second session — so the registration and login pages, the welcome and product tour, and a new app shell (Header, Sidebar, collapsible navigation) were rewritten end to end, with layout logic pulled out of the dashboard page into a real shell. Shipped as one 27-file, ~2,500-line change.

Hardened the top of the funnel without taxing real users. Cloudflare Turnstile now sits across sign-up, sign-in and password reset, behind an environment flag that lets captcha no-op cleanly in local development when no key is configured — so bot abuse stops at the door while the team's own auth call signatures stay untouched.

Turned activation from a screen into a system. Drove the onboarding checklist and product tour through several rounds: closed a race condition in visited-page tracking, rebuilt the checklist to derive completion state fresh on every render so progress stopped going stale when users switched workspaces, then shipped Onboarding 2.0, which persists tour progress and workspace-setup state to the backend so a returning user picks up exactly where they left off.

Made the AI agent believable. Velo AI is the whole reason a buyer signs up, and the side drawer is where they watch it work. Added task persistence so in-progress and completed runs survive a closed drawer or a tab switch, and killed a bug that pinned every past agent action in view instead of the one just selected — the difference between an assistant that looks in control and one that looks confused.

Shortened the path from AI output to real work. Redesigned Jira ticket creation, collapsing a multi-tab modal into a single user-story-first flow, and added the ability to save tickets internally without exporting to Jira, with a clickable detail view — so a team can evaluate what the agent produced before committing it to their board. Consolidated metadata handling that had been copy-pasted across components into two shared utility libraries.

Replaced the demo-ware. Dashboard summary cards now render live workspace data instead of placeholder content, and initiative tracking filters by status, owner and ticket type through a dedicated toolbar filter menu, with the query and filtering logic behind it.

Delivered the core pitch in code. Velociti sells strategy that stays connected to execution automatically; VPD-607 made that literally true. A completed Prototype or Context Loop job, or a newly created ticket, now advances an Initiative's status, which cascades to its linked Strategy Theme — and a manual status change on a tracked ticket cascades upward the same way. Wired the automation to wait on the real job-completion signal rather than racing the initial API call, and added cache invalidation so recent activity on the dashboard reflects the change immediately.

Went where the agents run. On the FastAPI + LangGraph backend: added design-asset packaging to Context Loop exports so generated PRDs carry their design context through the full pipeline, normalized inconsistent LLM content-block response shapes that were breaking downstream parsing on certain model outputs, and trimmed oversized DynamoDB log entries written by the export workflow.

And into the data layer. On Supabase: wrote the migration and edge function support for a new deferred initiative status, added a shared Gemini-backed user story generation function, and renamed the Context PRD concept to Context Loop consistently across edge functions to match the renamed frontend feature.

Shipped features with their tests attached. Nearly every feature landed with automated coverage in the same commit — 100 to 250+ lines at a time — across checklist state derivation, Jira ticket creation and export, Velo AI drawer behavior and initiative status automation.

Made the stack runnable. Stood up the full local development environment with Docker Compose for the FastAPI + LangGraph agents backend, and used the Supabase CLI to keep the local Postgres schema in sync with the remote project.

research_experience.title: Graduate Research — Activation Steering for Automatic Program Repair
research_experience.description: Applied and implemented a training-free activation steering technique (representation engineering, from published research) in PyTorch to improve CodeLLM reliability for bug-fixing. Hands-on work was tuning the steering strength per model across 40+ layer-and-strength configurations on an HPC Slurm cluster, and evaluating on HumanEval and Defects4J across CodeLlama and Qwen. No model weights were retrained.
research_experience.plain_summary: I took an existing method called activation steering — nudging a model's internal signals as it generates, without retraining it — and applied it to two open-source coding models, CodeLlama and Qwen. My hands-on work was dialing in the steering strength for each model and testing it against a standard coding benchmark (HumanEval) and a set of real-world software bugs (Defects4J) until the models produced more correct, reliably compiling code. It raised first-try success by about 8 points on CodeLlama and cut invalid, non-compiling output to near zero, holding across both model families.
research_experience.contribution_scope: Applied and tuned a published technique; the method itself (activation steering / representation engineering) is prior work, not my own invention.
research_experience.novel_finding: Middle transformer layers optimal for code generation tasks; late layers optimal for repair tasks — suggesting task-dependent reasoning stages in CodeLLM architecture.

projects.name: Personal AI Agent System (Hermes)
projects.description: Four progressively connected projects that turned a local AI agent into a personal assistant. First: installed it on Windows for free using a model from OpenRouter. Second: made it reachable from an iPhone anywhere via a private VPN. Third: wired it to Gmail and Google Calendar so it can read, draft, and send on command with a confirmation step before anything goes out. Fourth: taught it a custom skill that compiles a weekly digest of GitHub commits and calendar events and delivers it automatically every Friday.

phases.phase_1_setup: Installed Hermes Agent v0.18.2 on Windows, connected the nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b free model through OpenRouter, and ran the terminal TUI. Prompted the agent to build a Pomodoro timer app — it used 27 tools autonomously and produced a working app. Exported the full session as a JSONL audit log.
phases.phase_2_mobile: Launched Hermes WebUI via bootstrap.py with HERMES_WEBUI_HOST set to 0.0.0.0 so the server accepted LAN connections. Configured Tailscale to create a private mesh network between the Windows machine and iPhone. Installed Hermex on iOS to reach the agent from anywhere on the tailnet.
phases.phase_3_google_workspace: Created a Google Cloud project, enabled Gmail API, Google Calendar API, and Google People API, and completed the OAuth2 flow. Fixed a Testing mode blocker by adding the account as an approved test user in the OAuth consent screen. Used natural language to search, read, and send emails, with the agent waiting for manual confirmation before delivery. Created calendar events using timezone-aware ISO 8601 timestamps.
phases.phase_4_skill_automation: Connected GitHub to the agent through the MCP GitHub server with a tools.include list to limit active tools and preserve context. Found that raw API access alone produced generic responses with no structure. Authored a custom SKILL.md that gave the agent procedural formatting rules: pull GitHub commits and calendar events, filter noise, and compile a structured Markdown weekly review. Scheduled it to run autonomously every Friday at 5 PM UTC (cron: 0 17 * * 5), delivering results directly to the Hermex mobile app.

engineering_notes: tools.include in the Hermes config restricts which MCP tools are active, keeping context focused and reducing token waste
SKILL.md files give the agent explicit procedural rules — without them, it defaults to generic clarifying questions rather than taking structured action
Setting HERMES_WEBUI_HOST to 0.0.0.0 is what allows Tailscale devices to reach the locally running WebUI
OAuth2 testing mode blocks all accounts by default; adding the account as an approved test user in the Google Cloud Console consent screen is required before the flow can complete
highlights: Agent built a working Pomodoro timer app autonomously using 27 tools in one session
Mobile-accessible agent anywhere on the tailnet via Tailscale and Hermex iOS
Gmail and Calendar connected via OAuth2 with human-in-the-loop confirmation before any email send
Custom weekly-review skill pulls GitHub commits and calendar data, compiles a structured Markdown report, and runs every Friday via cron

projects.name: AI English Speaking Trainer
projects.description: An English speaking coach that runs entirely in the browser with no app install required. The user picks casual conversation practice or a mock interview for a specific role, speaks through the microphone, and hears the AI trainer reply aloud. projects.architecture: Express.js 5 backend with three POST endpoints: start, turn, and evaluate. Conversation state lives in Gemini's Interactions API via previous_interaction_id, removing the need to forward a growing history array on every turn. The evaluate endpoint attaches a JSON Schema to the request, so Gemini returns a parseable structured report with no string parsing on the server.
engineering_notes: Three-model fallback chain (primary then two backups) keeps the app running if one Gemini model is unavailable
JSON Schema on the evaluation request guarantees structured output with typed fields: overallScore, categoryScores, corrections, strengths, nextSteps
Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition + SpeechSynthesis) handles voice input and audio output entirely in the browser with no third-party speech service
Input sanitization on all endpoints: conversation history capped at 20 turns and 2,000 chars per turn; role field normalized and capped at 100 chars
highlights: Stateful multi-turn conversation via Gemini Interactions API — no manual context window management
Structured coaching report with 4 scored categories, corrections, strengths, and next steps
In-browser voice input and AI voice output with no paid speech APIs
Three-model fallback chain for API reliability

research_paper.title: Automatic Program Repair Through Activation Steering
research_paper.subtitle: A Research Project on Enhancing Code Generation through Neural Network Steering
research_paper.abstract_summary: Training-free method for improving CodeLLM reliability using Activation Steering (Representation Engineering). Computes a correctness vector from contrastive buggy/correct code pairs and injects it into residual streams via PyTorch forward hooks at inference time.

benchmarks.Defects4J: 565 real-world Java bugs (pass@1 against full test suite)

novel_findings: Code correctness is a steerable, linearly-represented concept in CodeLLM activation space
Middle layers optimal for generation tasks (HumanEval); late layers optimal for repair tasks (Defects4J)
Activation steering eliminates invalid/non-compiling output without any model retraining
limitations: Requires white-box model access (not usable with GPT-4 API)
Hyperparameter grid search needed per new model
